title: Householder logical experts from one shared FFN
hypothesis: Sixteen expert-specific Householder output Views over one shared two-layer FFN can match independent experts with much lower bytes and modest added compute; a same-budget FiLM control tests whether simple diagonal gains explain the function diversity.
mirror_coordinate: per-expert products of r Householder output reflections
logical_multiplicity: 16 routed logical experts over one physical FFN
controls: native Householder/BOFT-style orthogonal parameterization with identical function

development.selection_metric: per-expert output NRMSE, pairwise output diversity, actual serialized bytes, and active expert MAC proxy

success_gate: Across all audit seeds, Householder output NRMSE <=1e-5 and complete payload <=25% independent at r<=4; active compute <=1.2x independent at r<=4. Compare same-budget FiLM output error. Native exact alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific attribution.
failure_gate: Any audit seed exceeds quality/byte/compute thresholds at r<=4 or a simpler FiLM control matches quality with lower bytes/compute. Exact native Householder alias rejects Mirror-specific attribution regardless of generic expert-sharing feasibility.
boundaries: Synthetic routed FFN outputs only; no expert-training optimization, language-model utility, or GPU throughput claim.
Teacher experts are generated from the Householder family by construction; this is a representation feasibility experiment, not learned capacity.
One chosen expert is active per sample; router assignment IDs are serialized and charged.
